defensiveAbilities.name: Erosion Aura
defensiveAbilities.description:
120 feet.

The guthallath erodes away the physical integrity of all around it. Creatures and objects in the emanation other than the guthallath have their Hardness and resistances reduced by 10.

At the start of their turn, a creature in the erosion aura's area takes 6d6 Bludgeoning Damage damage with a Basic DC 39 Fortitude Saving Throw save.

defensiveAbilities.name: Immunity to Magic
defensiveAbilities.description: The guthallath is immune to spells of 6th rank or lower and activations of magic items of 13th level or lower.

offensiveAbilities.name: Annihilation Beams
offensiveAbilities.description:
A guthallath releases two beams of destruction from its eyes. Each beam is a 120ft Line. Everything in either line takes 13d10 Untyped Damage damage with a Basic DC 41 Fortitude Saving Throw save.

A creature reduced to 0 HP is reduced to a fine powder as the Disintegrate spell. There is no additional effect on creatures in any area where the beams overlap.

The guthallath can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.

offensiveAbilities.name: Deadly Throw
offensiveAbilities.description:
Requirements The guthallath has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect The guthallath throws the creature into the air, 100 feet high and 50 feet away. If the flung creature lands on another creature, the creature it lands on takes the same amount of bludgeoning damage.

The creature being landed on can attempt a Basic DC 41 Reflex Saving Throw save.

offensiveAbilities.name: Powerful Blows
offensiveAbilities.description: If a guthallath hits with an attack and rolls a natural 19 on the d20 roll, the attack is a critical hit. This has no effect if the 19 would be a failure.

offensiveAbilities.name: Trample
offensiveAbilities.description:
Huge or smaller, foot, Basic DC 45 Reflex Saving Throw

See rules...

The monster Strides up to double its Speed and can move through the spaces of creatures of the listed size, Trampling each creature whose space it enters. The monster can attempt to Trample the same creature only once in a single use of Trample. The monster deals the damage of the listed Strike, but trampled creatures can attempt a basic Reflex save at the listed DC (no damage on a critical success, half damage on a success, double damage on a critical failure).

offensiveAbilities.name: Improved Grab
offensiveAbilities.description:
See rules...

Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Improved Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with as a free action. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead spend an action to use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.

offensiveAbilities.name: Improved Knockdown
offensiveAbilities.description:
See rules...

Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Improved Knockdown in its damage entry

Effect The monster attempts to Trip the creature as a free action. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the monster's multiple attack penalty.

offensiveAbilities.name: Improved Push 20 feet
offensiveAbilities.description:
See rules...

The monster can use Push as a free action triggered by a hit with its initial attack.

lv3spells.name: Haste (Constant)
lv3spells.description:
Magic empowers the target to act faster. It gains the Quickened condition and can use the extra action each round only for Strike and Stride actions.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 6 creatures.

lv8spells.name: Truesight (Constant)
lv8spells.description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).
